prompts.habits.small.short: Break this task into small 10–15 minute steps: [task]
prompts.habits.small.detailed: I'm finding it hard to start: [task]. Break it into 10–15 minute steps. Make the first one very easy, something I can do right now. For each step, what will be done at the end. Mark good places to stop and pick up later.
prompts.habits.small.refine: Step [number] still feels big. Split it.
prompts.habits.small.check: I've done steps [numbers]. What's next, and how much is left?
prompts.habits.habit.short: Help me gently start a habit: [habit]
prompts.habits.habit.detailed: I want this habit: [habit]. Right now I do it [how often]. Make a gentle 4-week plan: start very small, what to attach it to (after which daily routine), how to track progress, what to do after a missed day. No strict rules or guilt.
prompts.habits.habit.refine: Week [number] didn't work out. How can I simplify the plan rather than give up?
prompts.habits.habit.check: Here's how the 2 weeks went: [how it went]. What's working and what should change?
prompts.habits.reminders.detailed: Write 10 short phone reminders for [task]. Tone: calm, no pressure or blame, no “you forgot again”. Vary the wording so they don't get stale. Each up to 8 words. Add 2 encouraging ones for when it's done.
prompts.habits.reminders.refine: Add a little humour, but no sarcasm.
prompts.habits.reminders.check: What time of day is best for a [task] reminder, given my day looks like this: [routine]?
prompts.habits.done.short: Help me make a list of what I got done this week: [notes]
prompts.habits.done.detailed: Here are my notes for [period]: [notes]. Make a done list grouped by area (study, work, home, health, people, for myself). Include small things that usually go unnoticed. End with one sentence on what went best. Don't add anything of your own.
prompts.habits.done.refine: Which of these did I do regularly? Are any already becoming habits?
prompts.habits.done.check: Ask me 3 questions about the past week to help me notice what I learned.
prompts.habits.balance.short: Help me alternate study and rest for the day: [tasks]
prompts.habits.balance.detailed: Today I need to do: [tasks]. I have [hours] hours. Make a schedule that alternates: 25–50 minute work blocks, short breaks with movement or fresh air, one longer meal break, time for something enjoyable. Hard tasks first, while I have energy.
prompts.habits.balance.refine: Suggest 10 ideas for a 5-minute break without my phone.
prompts.habits.balance.check: I'm already tired by [time]. How should I rearrange the rest of the day?
prompts.habits.obstacles.short: What's getting in the way of my goal [goal], and how can I deal with it?
prompts.habits.obstacles.detailed: My goal: [goal]. What usually gets in the way: [obstacles]. Table: obstacle, why it happens (ask me if unclear), 2 ways around it, how to tell if a method is working. No blaming or shaming: I want practical solutions.
prompts.habits.obstacles.refine: Obstacle [number] involves other people. How can I talk to them about it?
prompts.habits.obstacles.check: I tried [method] and here's what happened: [result]. Keep going or change?
prompts.habits.start.short: Suggest 7 ways to get started when I don't feel like it: [task]
prompts.habits.start.detailed: I need to do [task] but keep putting it off. Suggest 8 different ways to start: a 5-minute timer, starting in the middle, changing location, arranging it with someone, doing the most pleasant part first, and others. For each, when it helps most. No lecturing.
prompts.habits.start.refine: Why might I be putting off this particular thing? Ask me 3 questions to figure it out.
prompts.habits.start.check: I started and did [what I did]. How do I keep the momentum?
prompts.habits.return.short: How do I get back to [activity] after a [time] break?
prompts.habits.return.detailed: I used to do [activity] regularly, then took a [time] break because of [reason, optional]. Make a 2-week plan to get back: what amount to start with (less than before), how to increase gradually, how not to compare myself with my old level, what to do if I slip again.
prompts.habits.return.refine: Make the plan even gentler: I don't have much energy.
prompts.habits.return.check: A week has passed: [how it went]. Can I step it up or is it too soon?
prompts.habits.reflect.short: Give me 7 questions to reflect on the past [week, month, term].
prompts.habits.reflect.detailed: Write 10 reflection questions for [period]: what went well, what was hard, what I learned, what brought joy, what to keep, what to change, what I can thank myself for. Open, kind questions without judgement.
prompts.habits.reflect.refine: Make a short 3-question version for every evening.
prompts.habits.reflect.check: Here are my answers: [answers]. What one small step for next week follows from them?
prompts.habits.limits.short: Make a schedule that works within these limits: [limits]
prompts.habits.limits.detailed: Help me build a weekly schedule. Constraints: [limits, e.g. commute time, work, caring for a relative, low energy in the evenings]. Must-dos: [tasks]. Nice-to-haves: [optional]. Table by day. Must-dos first, then nice-to-haves only if there's room. Leave some gaps.
prompts.habits.limits.refine: I usually have less energy on [day]. Redistribute things.
prompts.habits.limits.check: Which nice-to-haves still don't fit? What should I do with them: move, shrink or drop?

verify.habits.small: The first step should be so easy it's silly not to do it. If it feels daunting, break it down further.
verify.habits.habit: Habits take weeks to form. Missing a day is normal: what matters is coming back, not being perfect.
verify.habits.reminders: Too many reminders stop being noticed. Start with one or two.
verify.habits.done: A done list is for you, not for a report. Include even small things.
verify.habits.balance: If you're constantly drained even after rest, talk to someone close or a doctor.
verify.habits.obstacles: The AI's solutions are generic. Pick the ones that fit your life and try them one at a time.
verify.habits.start: Not every method suits everyone. Try 2–3 and keep what works for you.
verify.habits.return: After a break it's normal to restart smaller than before. That isn't a step back.
verify.habits.reflect: The answers are for you alone. Don't paste anything into the chat you're not comfortable sharing.
verify.habits.limits: You know your limits best. If the schedule doesn't fit, the schedule is wrong, not you.
